note: kind=image means a final static illustration/screenshot; kind=gif means a final animated demonstration. All newly planned visuals currently render the same placeholder PNG. Caption copy is reader-facing.

slots.alt: Focus controls displayed in the Unreal Engine World Outliner
slots.caption: Focus adds compact controls alongside Actors, keeping visibility and protection decisions within the Outliner.

slots.alt: Diagram of Focus integrations with Unreal Engine editor systems
slots.caption: The Focus Editor module coordinates Outliner widgets, editor interaction guards, viewport filtering and Actor state.

slots.alt: Focus plugin folder installed in an Unreal Engine project
slots.caption: A project installation places the Focus plugin folder directly beneath the project’s Plugins directory.

slots.alt: Animation showing Focus controls being enabled and used for the first time
slots.caption: The initial workflow reveals the Focus column, adjusts its visible categories and applies an action to a test Actor.

slots.alt: Diagram showing Focus evaluating a selected Outliner row and its eligible Actors
slots.caption: A row’s quick-action state is derived from the eligible loaded Actors in its resolved scope.

slots.alt: Focus Quick Actions category menu in the World Outliner
slots.caption: The category menu controls which of the ten Quick Actions groups appear in the Outliner column.

slots.alt: Side-by-side comparison of Hide in Editor and Hidden in Game
slots.caption: Hide in Editor changes the editing view, while Hidden in Game configures a separate native Actor property.

slots.alt: Diagram of Solo filtering visible primitives in an Unreal Editor viewport
slots.caption: Solo narrows the editor view to selected primitive scene IDs without rewriting the hidden state of unrelated Actors.

slots.alt: Focus protection widget displaying different lock levels across a folder
slots.caption: A mixed protection state shows that eligible Actors do not currently share the same protection level.

slots.alt: Diagram of Focus selection, transform, command and Details editing guards
slots.caption: Focus enforces its editing protections through multiple native editor integration paths rather than a single global lock.

slots.alt: Simulation Quick Actions micro-widget showing its six controls
slots.caption: The Simulation category exposes physics, gravity, impulse and asynchronous ticking settings in one compact group.

slots.alt: Animation of a mesh being configured for physics and gravity using Focus
slots.caption: An eligible movable mesh can be configured to simulate physics and respond to world gravity through separate controls.

slots.alt: Diagram distinguishing Actor-scoped and Primitive Component-scoped simulation controls
slots.caption: Async Physics Tick applies to Actors, while the remaining Simulation controls target compatible Primitive Components.

slots.alt: Physics Events micro-widget showing hit, overlap and wake event controls
slots.caption: The Physics Events category exposes the three native notification settings for eligible primitive components.

slots.alt: Animation showing overlap generation being enabled and tested in Play
slots.caption: Overlap notifications require a compatible collision setup as well as the Generate Overlap Events setting.

slots.alt: Diagram of primitive collision and physics event generation paths
slots.caption: Hit, overlap and wake notifications originate from distinct native properties and require corresponding engine conditions.

slots.alt: Lighting Quick Actions category displaying channels and shadow settings
slots.caption: Lighting Channel 0, 1 and 2 can be adjusted independently of the Cast Shadows setting.

slots.alt: Comparison showing a light and selected meshes sharing a lighting channel
slots.caption: Matching channel selections allow compatible lights and primitives to interact without changing the other channel flags.

slots.alt: World Quick Actions showing main-world, editor-only, spatial-loading and HLOD flags
slots.caption: The World category places four Actor-level configuration choices directly in the Outliner.

slots.alt: World Partition example showing an Actor’s spatial-loading setting
slots.caption: Spatial loading is an Actor configuration decision whose result depends on the surrounding World Partition setup.

slots.alt: Diagram showing World Quick Actions flowing to Actor properties and engine subsystems
slots.caption: Focus updates native Actor flags; World Partition, HLOD generation and cooking interpret those flags independently.

slots.alt: Network Quick Actions displaying the available replication-related settings
slots.caption: Network actions expose three specific native configuration values without replacing the rest of Unreal’s replication setup.

slots.alt: Diagram showing Actor-level and Primitive Component-level network property targets
slots.caption: The Network category uses different target scopes for Actor loading, movement replication and physics-to-proxy settings.

slots.alt: Navigation Quick Actions displaying the navigation contribution and obstacle flags
slots.caption: The Navigation category exposes native component settings that influence how Unreal builds and updates navigation data.

slots.alt: Animation comparing navmesh results before and after changing navigation contribution
slots.caption: Disabling navigation contribution on selected collision can remove its influence after Unreal updates the navigation data.

slots.alt: Mobility micro-widget showing its Static, Stationary and Movable choices
slots.caption: The three vertically arranged Mobility choices map directly to Unreal’s native Scene Component mobility values.

slots.alt: Animation applying Movable to eligible Scene Components with Focus
slots.caption: Changing Mobility across a selected scope prepares eligible components for workflows that require movement.

slots.alt: LOD Quick Actions displaying Forced LOD and distance-culling options
slots.caption: The LOD category combines mesh LOD selection with two separate distance-culling flags.

slots.alt: Animation of click, Alt-click, mouse-wheel and double-click input on Forced LOD
slots.caption: The Forced LOD value can be stepped directly or entered numerically, with zero restoring automatic LOD selection.

slots.alt: Diagram comparing a requested Forced LOD value against a mesh’s available authored LODs
slots.caption: Focus checks the authored LOD range and indicates when a requested forced level exceeds a target mesh’s available data.

slots.alt: Diagram comparing category visibility, control colors and persistence options
slots.caption: Visibility controls the Outliner layout, colors communicate state, and persistence determines which Focus edits are saved.

slots.alt: Focus category visibility menu with several Quick Actions groups enabled
slots.caption: The header menu lets each editor user choose which Quick Actions categories occupy space in their Outliner.

slots.alt: Focus controls showing enabled, disabled, mixed, unavailable and alert colors
slots.caption: Distinct visual states help differentiate active settings, mixed selections, unavailable properties and important warnings.

slots.alt: Animation changing Solo persistence and temporarily isolating Actors
slots.caption: With Solo configured as session-only, the editing view can be isolated without replacing the previously saved Solo state.

slots.alt: Diagram of Focus temporarily restoring persistent Actor values during package serialization
slots.caption: During a package save, Focus substitutes recorded persistent values for active session-only native changes before restoring the live editor state.

slots.alt: Animation restoring temporarily hidden, Soloed and protected Actors
slots.caption: Restore Temporary Changes reverts tracked session-only Focus edits while leaving unrelated persistent changes intact.

slots.alt: Outliner hierarchy showing a loaded folder, attachments and mixed selected Actors
slots.caption: A Quick Action can apply across eligible loaded members of a folder, group, attachment hierarchy or selection.

slots.alt: Animation applying Selection and Transform Lock to a completed Outliner folder
slots.caption: Bulk protection makes finished environment content harder to select or transform accidentally during adjacent work.

slots.alt: Diagram of row scope resolution across folders, attachments, groups and selected Actors
slots.caption: Focus resolves its action targets from loaded Actor relationships rather than only from Outliner rows currently visible on screen.

slots.alt: Architecture diagram linking the Focus module, Outliner column, editor guards and view extension
slots.caption: The editor module coordinates presentation, input protection, state persistence and view filtering through Unreal’s native interfaces.

slots.alt: Diagram of Focus user settings, Actor package metadata and native Actor properties
slots.caption: Focus stores preferences separately from Actor state, while native quick properties remain part of the Actor and Component data they modify.

slots.alt: Comparison of Mixed and Not Applicable states in Focus’s Outliner column
slots.caption: Mixed indicates differing eligible values, while Not Applicable indicates that the target lacks an editable matching property.

slots.alt: Focus control tooltip explaining why a micro-widget is unavailable for an Actor
slots.caption: Eligibility tooltips help distinguish unavailable properties from controls that are simply switched off.

slots.alt: Focus release folder located inside an Unreal Engine project’s Plugins directory
slots.caption: Replacing the full Focus folder while Unreal is closed avoids mixing files from incompatible plugin releases.

slots.alt: Timeline showing Focus v1.0, v2.0 and planned v3.0 capabilities
slots.caption: Focus evolved from Visual and Interaction controls in v1.0 to broader native Quick Actions in v2.0, with extensibility planned for v3.0.

slots.alt: Conceptual architecture of Focus categories, third-party providers and the Quick Widget Builder
slots.caption: The planned extension registry would provide a shared foundation for built-in actions, plugin contributions and user-authored widgets.
